stem: A legacy application whose source code cannot be modified runs on a fleet of four EC2 instances in one Region behind a single DNS name. A solutions architect must add automated, health-checked failover that stops sending requests to any unhealthy instance without depending on DNS changes reaching clients. Which addition meets this?

choices.text: An Application Load Balancer or Network Load Balancer placed in front of the fleet, with health checks removing unhealthy targets from rotation.
Use Amazon Route 53 failover routing with health checks, pointing at a single instance as the primary endpoint.
Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to replicate the servers into a staging area for a future failover.
Use RDS Proxy to pool the application's database connections.

rationale: A load balancer placed in front of the existing fleet adds health-checked, automated failover between targets without touching the application itself, which is exactly what a legacy, unmodifiable codebase needs. Route 53 failover routing also needs no code change, but it fails over by changing DNS answers, so clients keep using the old record until its TTL expires, which misses the no-DNS-propagation requirement; pointed at a single primary instance it also does not spread requests across the four-instance fleet the way a load balancer does. AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates whole servers for a Regional disaster failover; it is not the mechanism that health-checks and routes everyday traffic between targets. RDS Proxy pools and manages database connections; it does not health-check or route application traffic between servers, so it does not add the failover this design needs.
